full_judgment:
17. In support of the contentions Shah Wali Vs. Ghulam Din alias Gaman and Muhammad 19 DLR SC 143 and Bangladesh and another Vs. Md. Salimullah and others 35 DLR AD 1 had been relied upon. The proposition of law enunciated in the said two authorities is that operation of a decree passed by a court of first instance is not automatically suspended on the mere filing of an appeal before the appellate court. 

 27. Keeping in view the spirit of the language used in Rule 5 of Order 41 read with Rule 2 of Order 43 of the Code it becomes manifestly clear execution of a decree or an order shall not be stayed automatically by reason only of an appeal having been preferred from any decree or order and the same having been preferred from any decree or order and the same having been admitted court of appeal of course showing sufficient cause record an order of staying the operation of any decree or order on the strength of Rule 5 of Order 41 and Rule 2 of Order 43 of the Code of Civil Procedure. For the view taken 1 am fortified with two authorities placed before me from the side of petitioner: Shah Wali vs Ghulam Din alias Gaman and Muhammad, 19 DLR SC143 and Bangladesh and another Vs. Md. Salimullah and others 35 DLR. From the order under challenge it reveals that before recording order of stay there was nothing on record manifesting that learned District Judge had been satisfied for sufficient cause in recording an order of stay and the said order is eminently an unjust order. Learned District Judge, thus, appears to have committed a grave error in staying the force and operation of the judgment and order dated 13.4.2000 recorded by learned Assistant Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka (practically learned District Judge stayed the force and operation of the learned Court). I am inclined to exercise revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in exercise of that power I quash the order under challenge in Revision staying the force and operation of the judgment and order dated 13.4.2000 passed by learned Assistant Judge. The contentions pressed into service from the side of the petitioners and the first branch of contention canvassed on behalf of the opposite parties, thus, stands disposed of.
